theses.thesis: T1: Operating leverage keeps margins expanding, because operating and SG&A cost growth stays well below revenue growth.
theses.signpost: FY2026 operating margin above 43.4% in the FY2026 10-K (filed about February 2027). Invalidation: below 40.6%, or restructuring rising again without a matching margin gain.

theses.thesis: T2: The share price assumes growth well above consensus, so at consensus growth the implied return falls short of the cost of capital.
theses.signpost: FY2026 revenue growth of at least 9% in the FY2026 10-K (about February 2027). Invalidation: FY2026 revenue growth of 12% or more.

theses.thesis: T3: Deleveraging continues, but payouts near 94% of free cash flow will limit further debt reduction.
theses.signpost: FY2026 total debt below $7.35 billion, with buybacks plus dividends at or below free cash flow, in the FY2026 10-K. Invalidation: total debt above $7.35 billion, or payouts above free cash flow for a second consecutive year.

theses.thesis: T4: Debt-issuance cyclicality will show up in MIS earnings within a year, so the stock is exposed to a weaker issuance cycle.
theses.signpost: Corporate Finance (CFG) revenue growth of at least 5% in FY2026, against 9% in FY2025, reported in the FY2026 10-K. Invalidation: CFG revenue growth at or above 9% in FY2026 even if debt issuance is flat. CFG is not reported separately in the 10-Q excerpts, so MIS external revenue is used as the proxy.
